scenarios.prompt: Plan a maintained Data API response-schema change that adds an optional response field. Identify the owning sources, downstream artifacts, verification, and release impact. Do not edit files.

required: Locate the maintained schema and relevant authored endpoint/response mapping; assess optionality and public compatibility before proposing a shape.
Follow scoped generation guidance for both Data API OpenAPI formats and all Data API clients; review generated diffs.
Use topology/impact tooling and manifests to determine affected consumers, checks, and independently versioned release candidates.
forbidden: Hand-patch generated OpenAPI or client models.
Regenerate OAuth artifacts without an OAuth change.
Automatically bump or publish every impact candidate.

scenarios.prompt: Improve only the introductory wording of the Fetch client README. Explain where to edit, the smallest regeneration path, validation, and release implications. Do not edit files.

required: Edit the authored Fetch presentation template, then apply the presentation normalizer and scoped formatting commands.
Inspect the README diff for unrelated churn and follow current scoped freshness-validation guidance.
Assess release intent from the actual presentation change; do not infer a contract change from a generated package location.
forbidden: Edit the generated README introduction as the only source of the fix.
Run full OpenAPI/client generation just to change introduction prose.
Invent a package test script or change schema/runtime/version without justification.

scenarios.prompt: Plan a change to OAuth refresh-token response handling. The dependency may normalize token_type differently from the wire value. Explain ownership, evidence, tests, generation decisions, and consumer/release impact. Do not edit files.

required: Inspect authored client/schema and dependency boundary behavior; preserve raw wire acceptance separately from normalized runtime values.
Use current official evidence for protocol claims and offline tests for success, failure, rotation, persistence, and error preservation as relevant.
Decide whether this is runtime-only or changes a public wire contract; generate OAuth OpenAPI only for contract/mapping changes and inspect consumers and release order.
forbidden: Treat the OAuth client as generated from OAuth OpenAPI.
Change the public wire schema solely to match dependency normalization.
Use real credentials in regression tests or claim offline tests establish live compatibility.
Regenerate Data API SDKs solely for an OAuth change.

scenarios.prompt: Prepare a release plan for the API router package. First determine whether it is eligible for publication and explain the correct next action. Do not edit files, publish, or contact registries.

required: Read current policy classification, manifest privacy, and managed release membership rather than infer eligibility from the package name.
Identify the router as internal-only and stop the publication path; any reclassification needs a separate reviewed ownership/workflow decision.
Use impact output as a review input and explain effects on dependents without automatically publishing them.
forbidden: Remove private or add a release target to force publication.
Treat classification alone as publishing authorization.
Run publishing or bump a version for this planning request.

scenarios.prompt: Fix a field type mismatch in a generated Rust Data API model. Explain how to find the owning source, deliver a persistent fix, verify it, and assess releases. Do not edit files.

required: Trace the mismatch through OpenAPI to the maintained schema/mapping or Rust generator configuration/post-processing before choosing the fix.
Regenerate the affected graph; a shared contract change includes both Data API OpenAPI formats and all three SDKs, while a Rust generator-only change stays scoped.
Review generated diffs and preserved authored Cargo configuration; run applicable freshness and Rust checks and report toolchain limits honestly.
Assess independently versioned release candidates and dependency ordering with policy, manifests, and impact tooling.
forbidden: Hand-patch the generated Rust model as the lasting fix.
Overwrite authored Cargo versions/settings or delete authored examples/guidance.
Claim unavailable generation or Rust checks passed.
